Q: trying to get away from AI as hard as possible but losing it sometimes A:

The thing that makes large language models work is the breadth of the text fed into them, more than any person will ever encounter in a lifetime. There's nothing wrong with taking advantage of that, any more than using a search engine that's catalogued more web sites than you will ever see.

I can only guess what you really dislike about using AI systems, but three things should help. First, don't use it as a substitute for thinking. Second, use it a resource for learning. Third, don't use AI as the only resource. I think that covers it.

Q: How do you make a default constructor and fix the type deduction error indicated by E3158 and E0289? A:

I am making several template classes and just realized that their non-initialized declarations give errors E3158 and E0289: indicating that my compiler cannot identify the class's template arguments.

test is the name of a class template and as such it need a template argument T for the template parameter arb so that test<T> becomes a class type.

The difference is important. Class-types can have an instance of that class-type but class templates can't have an instance as they're not a type!

There's no way for the compiler to infer the type of arb by itself.

I am wondering whether there is any way around this? Can I maybe force the default constructor to pick a type?

You can use a default argument for the template parameter arb if you think it should be used when no type for arb is specified as in:

//-----------------------vvv--->specify the default type here
template <typename arb = int>
class test{//...};
test t{}; //now this will work

Q: Why are there random files being generated at the root of my nextjs project when deploying on google cloud vm's ubuntu using nginx and pm2? A:

So apparent, it was due to the NextJS version that I was using for the project (which was 15.5.5), which has serious security issue. I'm not 100% sure how this work as I'm not really a security expert, but I believe this is the cause (as stated here https://nextjs.org/blog/CVE-2025-66478).

Once I saw this, I simply fix the issue by updating the NextJS version from 15.5.5 to 15.5.12, and the problem is gone (or at least I no longer see those weird files being generated in my server). Would need to continue monitoring to be sure if there's any issue, but for now it's resolved.

Q: AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'dtype' A:

The simple answer is that your data is not a numpy datatype. This is likely because the column isn't fully numeric (i.e. contains None or something).

The short solution:

print(np.nanmean(pd.to_numeric(illiq)))

The quickest way to solve this is to simply coerce the data to a numeric type that numpy likes. This can be done via pandas' to_numeric method.
